A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TinySQL work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching content moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning accuracies, circuit recovery experiments, ablations, SAE analyses and logit-lens findings, including substantial appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds a three-example logit-lens case study with token-rank results in Tables 19–20.

M1.justification: The dataset-generation procedure, model architectures, fine-tuning approach, EAP circuit extraction and SAE feature-selection algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix L adds analysis of existing models rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: The SQL complexity levels, language variants and general-capability evaluations are retained. The new case study uses existing CS2/CS3 tasks. The external-dataset statistics expand the documented comparison without establishing new model evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The EAP, SAE and size-matched random-circuit comparisons retain their participants, as do the base-versus-fine-tuned model comparisons. Newly cited datasets and synthetic-language studies are not added comparison methods.

E3.justification: New Appendix L adds a diagnostic on three BM2 examples using per-layer token ranks and the first layer attaining top rank. The existing data splits, training budgets, EAP sampling, ablation procedures and SAE settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds a focused case study examining keyword and schema-token emergence in COUNT, MIN and ORDER BY examples. This supplements the existing logit-lens plots; the corruption experiments, circuit-overlap analyses and head, MLP and full-layer ablations are retained.

E5.justification: EAP still uses 15 batches of 100 prompts and four synonym configurations, and random-circuit performance remains reported as averages. No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: v2 Appendix C.1's query-length averages of 12.91/26.52/41.76 are replaced by 16.48/38.76/42.39/53.73/61.61 for explicitly labelled CS1–CS5 synonym sets. v4 also adds external-dataset statistics and token-rank results in Tables 19–20. Matched model and circuit accuracies are unchanged; the relocated linguistic scores receive only rounding changes.

T1.justification: The EAP attribution approximation, normalized patching metric in Equation 1, SAE reconstruction objective and Algorithm 1 mathematics are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims: a progressive SQL interpretability testbed, identifiable and locally minimal circuits, and staged SQL generation. The added evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix L adds a finer interpretation separating basic SQL tokens, functional tokens and final-layer schema identifiers. Section 3.1 now describes TinySQL as lexically and semantically more challenging, dropping v2's qualification that concentrated synthetic table and field names may explain its linguistic statistics. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds explicit access pointers for the code and the dataset/model/SAE collection on page 2, plus the prompts, schemas and responses used in the new case study. Existing implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures are retained; the PDFs do not establish any change in the underlying training.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 add artificial-language and grammar-learning studies, CoSQL, SParC and MIMICSQL, and sharpen the motivation for studying multiple models and tasks. A lexical-density reference is added and the standalone BIRD reference is removed. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Background and dataset-statistics passages receive selective rewriting and reordering, affiliations are updated, and appendix statistics are consolidated into the main text. A new Appendix L moves the former logit-lens appendix to M. Most methodological, discussion and conclusion prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 Table 9 becomes an expanded main-text Table 1, and Tables 19–20 are added. Layer labels are corrected in the overlap and mean-ablation tables, floats are rearranged, and Figure 13 shrinks to one-column width. All original figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Resource-access pointers, an explicit dataset comparison and inspectable logit-lens examples modestly improve usability and evidential transparency. The gain is limited by errors in the new analysis: Table 19 gives COUNT's first top rank as layer 17 while Table 20 shows layer 16, and labels the ORDER BY example as GROUP BY. These weaken precise claims without overturning the examples' broader keyword-before-schema pattern; the less qualified dataset-difficulty interpretation also warrants caution.
